title: High-Performance Quasi-Solid Thermogalvanic Cells via Crown-Ether-Mediated Ion Migration

segments.text: As a sustainable energy technology, the thermogalvanic cell (TGC) shows great promise in harvesting low-grade thermal energy and converting it directly into usable electricity.
However, achieving a high output voltage for practical applications is still a great challenge.
Recent studies have focused on achieving higher thermovoltage by increasing the entropy change of redox couples.
The Soret effect (thermodiffusion) is often ignored in thermogalvanic systems.
The role of the counterion of the redox couple is overlooked.

Herein, we proposed that the thermovoltage of the quasi-solid thermogalvanic cell contained with K3Fe(CN)6/K4Fe(CN)6 can be increased by introducing 18-crown-6, a cationic selective complexing agent, amplifying the thermodiffusion of the cation.
Thanks to the synergistic combination of the Soret effect with the thermogalvanic effect, the corresponding Seebeck coefficient of the cell was greatly boosted from 1.26 to 2.22 mV/K.
The mechanism was analyzed systematically.
This work may offer a promising approach to promote the thermovoltage of TGC, facilitating low-grade energy harvesting.

title: Hydrogel incorporated with graphene oxide featuring enhanced thermosensitive crystallization for thermogalvanic cell

segments.text: Thermogalvanic cells (TGCs) have relatively high thermopowers originating from the thermogalvanic effect and can be used to convert low-grade heat into electricity.
Nevertheless, their restricted electrical output is insufficient for practical applications.
In this study, we present a graphene oxide (GO)-enhanced thermogalvanic hydrogel with [Fe(CN)6]4-/3-redox couple and guanidine hydrochloride (GdmCl).
GO serves as a nucleation template by adsorbing guanidinium ions, thereby inducing the crystallization of [Fe(CN)6]4-and enhancing the thermogalvanic effect.
As a result, the TGC using this hydrogel achieves a normalized power density of 700 mu W & sdot;m-2 & sdot;K-2 (Pmax@Delta T = 10 K) and a high thermopower of 3.2 mV & sdot;K-1.
Furthermore, the TGCs show the capability of harvesting thermal energy for operating small electronics and thermoelectric sensing.
This work represents a feasible strategy for the design and optimization of TGCs.

title: Material recognition and spatial thermal sensation enabled by organic thermogalvanic hydrogels

segments.text: Integrating thermal sensation into intelligent robotics is essential for advanced environmental perception and adaptive interaction.
Ionic thermoelectric hydrogels represent a promising avenue for next-generation thermal sensors, yet further improvements in sensitivity, structural design, and integration are needed.
Here, we present flexible, high-performance thermal sensor arrays based on organic thermogalvanic hydrogels, achieving a high sensitivity of 1.57 mV K-1 and a rapid response time of 0.4 s.
The enhanced sensing performance stems from the optimized thermopower in benzoquinone/hydroquinone (BQ/H(2)BQ) redox pairs and the highly reversible electrode reaction process.
The adopted hydrogel exhibits outstanding thermopower retention and wide operational temperature range (>50 degrees C), facilitated by ethylene glycol solvent exchange.
Leveraging integrated heating and sensing functionalities, the hydrogel thermal sensor arrays enable material recognition through machine learning analysis of thermal signatures.
Moreover, we demonstrate a high-density sensor array for mapping spatial temperature distributions generated by diverse heat sources.
This work establishes organic thermogalvanic hydrogels as a scalable platform for thermal sensing in next-generation robotics and wearable devices.

title: A rapidly moldable thermogalvanic organohydrogel for self-powered water temperature and level monitoring

segments.text: Thermogalvanic organohydrogel (TGHs) leverage the temperature difference (Delta T) to facilitate energy supply and electrical signal sensing without requiring external batteries.
The conventional preparation of thermogalvanic organohydrogel is often laborious and time-consuming, significantly hindering their widespread adoption and innovative applications.
Here, a novel preparation process was developed to fabricate our TGH sensor with a rapid prototyping based on the Hofmeister effect.
This process involved the combination of Fe3 + /2 + as the redox pair and poly(vinyl) alcohol (PVA) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) as the polymer network.
The development enabled rapid prototyping (<6 h), room temperature prototyping (similar to 25 degrees C) and high thermoelectric potential (0.86 mV/K).
Importantly, the Gel-Fe3+/2+ TGH was able to operate continuously in experiments at low temperatures(>-20 degrees C), together with excellent mechanical tensile properties.
This phenomenon was found to be attributable to the strong hydrogen bonds that were formed between DMSO and H2O.

Moreover, an e-skin device (smart finger cuffs) based on the Gel-Fe3+/2+ TGH technology has been demonstrated, capable of utilizing human waste heat to power wearable devices and rapidly detect the temperature (via Delta T-dependent voltage output) and volume (via multi-channel spatial voltage profiling) of water in a water cup.
Our work provides a new path for a novel green and safe method for rapid synthesis of TGH sensor, thus facilitating widespread use of TGHs for temperature detection in wearable electronic devices.
